proofs.full_local_argument: Fix any eligible feasible pair (x,y). For every v in Y, f(x,v)<=g(x,v)+delta; taking suprema yields sup_v f(x,v)<=sup_v g(x,v)+delta. For every u in X, f(u,y)>=g(u,y)-delta>=inf_w g(w,y)-delta; taking infima yields inf_u f(u,y)>=inf_u g(u,y)-delta. All four extrema are finite by assumption. Subtracting gives Gap_f(x,y)<=Gap_g(x,y)+2delta, and thus Gap_g<=eta implies Gap_f<=eta+2delta. For the specialization, y0 in Y and the diameter definition imply ||v-y0||<=D_y for every v in Y. Hence 0<=f(u,v)-g(u,v)=epsilon||v-y0||^2/(4D_y^2)<=epsilon/4 uniformly in u,v. Substituting delta=epsilon/4 and eta=epsilon/2 gives Gap_f<=epsilon. If f is continuous convex-concave on nonempty compact convex X,Y, g remains continuous convex-concave because the subtracted squared norm is concave in y and independent of x; extrema are attained, and Definition 4 applies. This is a local proof, not a quotation or author-named general theorem.

source_application.content: The source constructs g=f-epsilon||y-y0||^2/(4D_y^2), states uniform difference <=epsilon/4 and transfers an epsilon/2-saddle point of g to an epsilon-saddle point of f. The general comparison is curator-supplied local abstraction.

assumptions: A finite delta>=0 satisfies |f(u,v)-g(u,v)|<=delta for every (u,v) in X x Y.
At every pair where the conclusion is applied, all row suprema and column infima defining both gaps are finite real numbers; subtraction of infinities is excluded.
For the Eq.(4.1) specialization, Y is a bounded Euclidean set with diameter 0<D_y<infinity, y0 in Y, epsilon>0, and g(x,y)=f(x,y)-epsilon||y-y0||^2/(4D_y^2). Retain the finite-extrema requirement.
statement.conclusion: Gap_f(x,y)<=Gap_g(x,y)+2delta. In the Eq.(4.1) specialization delta=epsilon/4, so Gap_g<=epsilon/2 implies Gap_f<=epsilon. For continuous convex-concave objectives on the source's compact convex sets, this is the Definition 4 epsilon-saddle guarantee.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X,Y be nonempty sets and f,g:X x Y -> R. At a feasible pair (x,y), Gap_h(x,y)=sup_{v in Y}h(x,v)-inf_{u in X}h(u,y), for h=f,g.
statement.parameter_domains: delta,eta finite and nonnegative; specialization epsilon>0, 0<D_y<infinity. General comparison requires no convexity, smoothness or strong curvature.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such X,Y,f,g,delta and every eligible feasible pair, the deterministic comparison holds. For every eta>=0, Gap_g<=eta implies Gap_f<=eta+2delta.
